New Creation, Spirit Man, and the Healing of the Heart

Source note. The position attributed to Joshua James here is exactly as you described it: we are now spirit beings, we do not need heart healing, we only need the renewing of the mind. I could not find his own teaching publicly, so I treat this as a claim to be examined and I do not attribute any wording to him. For Jesudian Silvester, I can verify that he teaches about the Father's heart and identity in God, that his church lists vulnerability, combating shame, and holding stories as holy ground among its emphases, and that titles such as "Step by step process for your healing" and "Confession that heals" exist. I could not see how he answers this specific claim, so where I describe how his emphasis engages it, that is analysis, and a fill-in section is included for his actual words. Kruger is represented only by his well-documented Trinitarian, relational framework used throughout this series. Christians disagree on this topic, and this study says where.

PART 1: The Claim, Stated Fairly

The position can be broken into three propositions:

  1. Regeneration is complete. When you were born again, your spirit was made new, righteous, and whole (2 Cor 5:17).
  2. You are essentially your spirit. "You are a spirit, you have a soul, and you live in a body." Your true identity is the new spirit.
  3. Therefore the problem is only the mind. What remains is to renew the mind with truth (Rom 12:2). Talk of "healing the heart" or wounds misplaces the focus and keeps you stuck in the past.

1.1 What this position gets right

StrengthWhy it matters
Identity is settled in Christ, not earnedProtects against self-salvation and performance (Kruger's "self-salvation" strategy)
The new birth is real and total in its foundationJohn 3, Titus 3:5, Ephesians 2:5: God made us alive; this is not a mere improvement
Truth transforms (Rom 12:2)Beliefs shape emotions and behavior; this matches CBT/REBT and our belief-formation study
A warning against wound-identitySome inner-healing cultures leave people endlessly excavating pain and defining themselves by it
Encourages forward, faith-filled livingPhilippians 3:13: forgetting what lies behind and pressing forward

The question is not whether the new birth is real, or whether truth renews the mind. Both are. The question is whether these two truths exhaust what Scripture and human experience say about healing.

PART 2: What Do "Spirit," "Soul," "Heart," and "Mind" Mean?

Much of the disagreement rests on how these words are used. If "heart" and "mind" are different things, then "no heart healing, only mind renewal" is a coherent claim. If they overlap in Scripture, the sentence changes meaning.

TermBiblical usage (broadly)Note
Spirit (ruach, pneuma)The life-breath and the God-facing dimension of the person; made alive by the Spirit (Eph 2:5; Rom 8:10)The part most emphasized in "spirit man" teaching
Soul (nephesh, psyche)The whole living person, and often mind, will, and emotions (Gen 2:7; Ps 42:5; James 1:21)Scripture speaks of the soul being restored (Ps 23:3) and saved (1 Pet 1:9)
Heart (lev, kardia)The center of the person: thinking, feeling, desiring, and choosing all at once (Prov 4:23; Rom 10:10; Eph 1:18)In Hebrew thought, heart and mind are not separate compartments; the heart thinks
Mind (nous)Understanding, mindset, way of seeing (Rom 12:2; Eph 4:23 "the spirit of your mind")Eph 4:23 links spirit and mind in one phrase
Flesh / bodyEmbodied life, mortal, and the sphere of weakness (Rom 7–8)Redemption of the body is still awaited (Rom 8:23)

Two observations. (1) Christians hold different models: some see a threefold person (spirit, soul, body: 1 Thess 5:23), many see a unified whole with overlapping terms (Heb 4:12 shows they are distinct enough to divide only by God's word). Neither view supports treating the person as "only spirit." (2) Because heart and mind overlap in Scripture, "renewing the mind" is not clearly opposed to "healing the heart." Paul himself places renewal in "the spirit of your mind" (Eph 4:23) and prays for "the eyes of your heart" to be enlightened (Eph 1:18). Some writers even argue that a hard heart underlies a darkened mind (Eph 4:18), so the renewal of the mind involves the heart.

PART 3: Born Again and New Creation — What Actually Happened, and What Is Still Unfolding

3.1 What Scripture says has happened

RealityPassage

3.2 What Scripture says is still unfolding

Ongoing realityPassage
Put off the old self and be renewed in the spirit of your mindEphesians 4:22–24; Colossians 3:9–10 ("is being renewed")
Being transformed from glory to glory2 Corinthians 3:18

3.3 The pattern: indicative and imperative

Paul's letters consistently say "You are..." (indicative) and then "So become / put on / walk..." (imperative). The imperative is not an admission that the indicative failed. It is how the new identity comes to be lived out. This resolves the apparent puzzle: you are a new creation, and you are being renewed, both at once.

INDICATIVE: "You are new, included, adopted, alive"
↓
IMPERATIVE: "So put off, put on, be renewed, walk in it"
↓
EXPERIENCE catches up to identity in mind, emotions, body, and relationships

3.4 An illustration: Israel out of Egypt

God brought Israel out of Egypt in one act. They were free, legally and actually. Yet it took forty years, and a generation, before "Egypt" left them: the slave mentality, fear, complaining, and longing for old ways. Freedom was real; the renewal of the freed people's minds and hearts was a journey. Being born again is the exodus. Growth in Christ includes the wilderness.

PART 4: Does Scripture Speak of Healing the Heart and Soul?

PassageWhat it says
Psalm 147:3He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds
Psalm 23:3He restores my soul
Psalm 34:18The LORD is near to the brokenhearted
Isaiah 61:1–3; Luke 4:18Sent to bind up the brokenhearted; beauty for ashes
Proverbs 13:12; 17:22Hope deferred makes the heart sick; a crushed spirit dries the bones
Proverbs 4:23Guard your heart; everything flows from it
Hebrews 12:15A root of bitterness can spring up and defile many; believers are told to watch for it
1 Peter 2:11; James 1:21Passions war against the soul; the implanted word saves souls
1 Peter 2:24; Isaiah 53:5By His wounds you have been healed
John 21:15–19Jesus restores Peter with three questions for three denials: personal, relational heart restoration by a risen Lord
James 5:16; Galatians 6:1Confess and be healed; restore one another gently

Reading these fairly. One can say these are figures of speech for spiritual renewal, or that they refer to a healing that comes through truth alone. But the plain sense of many of them assumes that believers can be hurt, discouraged, embittered, and sick at heart, and that God, often through people, restores them. Peter's restoration is the clearest example: he was a born-again disciple who still needed his heart tended.

PART 5: The Human Reality — Why "Just Renew the Mind" Often Isn't Enough

5.1 What earlier studies showed

FindingSource in the seriesImplication
Shame and fear live in the body and nervous system, not only in thoughtEmotional-Neurological FrameworkCognitive truth alone does not reset an alarm system built by experience
Beliefs formed in relationship change most through relational experienceBelief and Character FormationSafe community is part of the mechanism, not an optional add-on
Knowing the I Am Not is not the same as being free of shameBreaking Shame studyTruth needs to be received and experienced
Hardened hearts result from repeated hurtHardened Hearts studyScripture itself names "heart of stone" and "heart of flesh"
Trauma requires safety, not merely insightEmotional-Neurological FrameworkProfessional and relational help are legitimate parts of healing

5.2 The risk of saying "you are only spirit; you don't need heart healing"

  • Spiritual bypassing. Pain is treated as a failure of faith, so it goes underground. Anxiety, depression, and trauma are labeled "unbelief."
  • New shame. "I am a perfect spirit, so why do I still struggle?" can produce the very shame the gospel heals.
  • Devaluing the body and emotions. If the person is "really" only spirit, then body and feelings feel like secondary or suspect. Scripture affirms creation and the body (Gen 1:31; 1 Cor 6:19; Rom 8:23).
  • Silencing lament. The Psalms and Jesus at Gethsemane and Lazarus' tomb show honest grief as part of faith.
  • Missing medical or trauma care. Some people need therapy, and saying "just renew your mind" can delay it.

5.3 The opposite risk, also real

  • Endless excavation. Turning every problem into a memory hunt.
  • Wound-identity. "I am my trauma" replaces "I am in Christ."
  • Passivity. Waiting to feel healed before living in faith.
  • Method over relationship. Techniques become a substitute for the Father.

The "renewing of the mind" emphasis is a needed corrective to these. The best answer holds both.

PART 6: Does the Relational Gospel Heal the Soul?

6.1 Kruger's framework overlaps with renewal of the mind

In Kruger's framework the deepest problem is the fallen mind: the lies (the I Am Nots) that make us believe we are outside the Father's love and start the self-salvation or escape projects. The cure is a renewed vision of the Father, Son, and Spirit, in whom we are included. So relational gospel and "renew the mind" are close allies. Where the relational gospel adds something is in how the mind is renewed.

6.2 "Knowing" in Scripture is relational

The renewal Paul describes is not only the addition of correct information. Biblical "knowing" (yada, ginosko) is relational and experiential: "that I may know Him" (Phil 3:10); eternal life is "that they know You" (John 17:3). A mind renewed by knowing a Person is renewed at the level of trust, attachment, and felt safety, which is where the heart lives.

Lie planted → I Am Not forms → insecure working model → self-supply → symptom
↓
Correctly named (mind)
↓
Trinity ministers: Father's love, Son's identity, Spirit's presence (relationship)
↓
Jesus' "I Am" replaces "I Am Not" (renewal of mind AND healing of the heart)
↓
Earned security; stewardship and community sustain it

In this pipeline "renewing the mind" and "healing the heart" are not two competing programs. They describe the same restoration seen from two angles: the mind seeing truly and the heart resting safely.

6.3 What "healing the soul" looks like in this view

AreaWhat heals it
Beliefs (mind)Truth, Scripture, naming lies, meditation on the Father's character
Emotions (heart)Being seen and received; honest lament; confession; forgiving and being forgiven
Body (nervous system)Safety, breath, movement, rest, sometimes therapy
RelationshipsSafe community, repair, boundaries
Will and habitsRepeated practice that expresses the new identity

PART 7: How Does Jesudian Tackle This?

What I can verify, and what I cannot. His teaching centers on the "love beat" of the Father's heart and on helping people understand identity in God. His ministry emphasizes vulnerability as a path to belonging, combating shame, fear and anxiety, honoring stories, and a relational lifestyle. Talks such as "Step by step process for your healing" and "Confession that heals" exist. I could not view their content, so I cannot say what he says about the "spirit being" claim. What follows is an analysis of how that emphasis would naturally engage it. Please add his actual statements.

7.1 How a Father's-heart, relational emphasis would likely engage the claim

Point of the claimWhere such an emphasis would agreeWhere it would likely press back
"You are a new creation in spirit"Yes. Identity and sonship are settled in ChristWould add that sonship is meant to be known and felt as a Father's love, not only affirmed as a doctrine
"Renew your mind"Yes. Truth must replace liesWould say the mind is renewed by encounter with the Father's heart, not by information alone
"No heart healing needed"Would agree that we should not live in the past or be defined by woundsWould likely say the heart carries real stories, hurts, and shame that need to be honored and healed in relationship (consistent with vulnerability, holy-ground stories, and shame work)
"You are already spirit; you're fine"Would affirm complete acceptanceWould likely warn against using it to skip honesty about pain, shame, or unresolved offense

Watch the healing message and record: (1) Does he speak of the heart as needing healing? In what terms? (2) How does he relate the new birth to ongoing healing? (3) What role does he give to renewing the mind? (4) What does he say about confession or vulnerability as part of that? (5) Does he address the "spirit being" teaching directly? PART 8: Reconciling "Spirit Man" with Born Again and New Creation

8.1 A layered model that honors both

DimensionStatus in ChristWhat is still unfolding
SpiritRegenerated, alive, united to Christ; complete in HimGrowing sensitivity and yielding to the Spirit
MindGiven the mind of Christ (1 Cor 2:16); truth availableRenewal of old patterns and lies (Rom 12:2)
Heart / emotionsNew heart given (Ezek 36:26)Wounds, hurts, shame, bitterness still need care (Ps 147:3; Heb 12:15)
BodyTemple of the Spirit (1 Cor 6:19)Awaiting redemption; carries stress and trauma responses
RelationshipsAdopted into the family (Eph 1:5)Learning to live in trust, repair, and love

8.2 The two sentences, both true

"You are a new creation; your spirit is alive and your identity is settled." and "You are being renewed in mind, healed in heart, and formed in body and relationship." The first is the foundation. The second is the house being lived in. To deny the first is to lose the foundation; to deny the second is to live in the doorway and never move in.

8.3 A further analogy

A child adopted at age six from an orphanage is legally and fully a son the day the papers are signed. Nothing more is required for sonship. Yet the child may hoard food, flinch at raised voices, and not believe the bed is his for years. The parents do not say, "You are a son, so you have no wounds; just think correctly." They also do not say, "You are your wounds." They say, "You are ours" and stay close while the child learns to live at home. That is what the relational gospel offers.

PART 9: Evaluating the Claim Fairly

Version of the claimAssessment
"Identity in Christ is complete, so start from acceptance, not from your wounds"Defensible and valuable. Matches the relational gospel's ground
"Renewing the mind is the central means of transformation"Strongly supported (Rom 12:2; Eph 4:23), if "mind" includes heart and relationship
"Believers should not define themselves by trauma or stay in endless inner-healing loops"Wise caution
"Believers do not have hearts that need healing, comfort, or restoration"Hard to reconcile with Psalm 147:3, Isaiah 61, Hebrews 12:15, John 21, and lived human experience
"We are only spirit beings"Not the biblical picture of the person, who is embodied and whose soul and body are also being redeemed

Questions to ask of any teaching on this: Does it make room for grief and lament? Does it distinguish identity from experience? Does it treat struggling believers with mercy? Does it include the body and community? Does it lead toward the Father, or toward technique or self-management? A teaching that answers these well is usually healthy whether it uses the language of "heart healing" or "mind renewal."

PART 10: Practical Integration

10.1 A daily rhythm that holds both

TimePracticeEmphasis

MiddayNotice a thought that contradicts it; replace it with truthMind renewal
EveningName honestly what you felt today; bring it to the Father; note any need to forgive or confessHeart

10.2 Which tool for which problem

SituationStart with
Recurring negative thought patternTruth-based mind renewal (identity declarations, cognitive reframing)
Emotion out of proportion; old memory triggeredHonest naming, safe person, co-regulation, possibly a counselor
Shame, hidden struggleConfession to God and a safe person

10.3 Two composite cases

Grace (composite). New in faith, Grace has panic attacks. She is told, "You are a spirit being; just confess your identity and renew your mind." She declares daily but still panics, and she starts to feel her faith is failing. A wise mentor tells her, "You are fully God's daughter, and your body is carrying real alarm from your history." Alongside her declarations she begins counseling and slow breathing practices and shares her story with one friend. Panic gradually decreases and the shame lifts. Lesson: identity plus care for heart and body.

Kevin (composite). Kevin has attended many inner-healing sessions and speaks mostly of his wounds. He feels more stuck each year. A pastor helps him anchor in who he is in Christ, practice truth daily, serve others, and use counseling sparingly and purposefully. His focus shifts from analyzing pain to living from acceptance. Lesson: renewal of mind as corrective to wound-identity.
